correctness.rationale: Use the exact selected current correction: for unit rows the squared-error drop is β(2−β)r_i². For z<1, the normalized mean 1−s+sz² decreases strictly in the weaker-row probability s, whose odds are maximized by the coordinatewise extreme stale multipliers e^(−ε), e^ε. No statistical independence of stale errors is used. Fresh and stale normalized means give the reported ratio. The loss equals (U−1)z^p(1−z²)/[(1+Uz^p)(1+z^(p+2))] and vanishes at 0 and 1. Its logarithmic derivative times z is the displayed strictly decreasing F on (0,1), which ranges from p to −∞; hence the unique zero gives the unique minimum. Invertibility realizes any prescribed nonzero residual pair for each fixed row system, without trajectory claims. With a=e^(−2ε), fixed z in (a,1) gives limit z² and thus limsup≤a². Any subsequential limit of minimizing z below a gives limiting ratio 1 because both weaker-row probabilities tend to zero; any limit at or above a gives liminf≥a² because the stale mean is at least z² and fresh at most 1. Both residuals zero is excluded as a zero-over-zero comparison; one zero gives ratio 1; p=0 or ε=0 is not in strict uniqueness scope. value.rationale: This is a natural robustness benchmark for adaptive row choice with imperfect relative scores and exact correction, separating a real source of progress loss from collisions or stale corrections. The unique worst imbalance and exact high-power limit give actionable quantitative meaning to the error budget in the smallest nontrivial system. It makes no unsupported asynchronous stability claim.
